#4199. 'The Best RPG I've Played This Year' - Queen's Domain Is A Low-Key GOTY Contender On Xbox

Back at the end of last month, a little-known RPG launched on Xbox in the form of Queen's Domain, which we highlighted in our October 30th new releases roundup alongside 14 other titles that arrived that day.

Ever since then, we've been hearing various bits of praise for the game across multiple platforms, and it's gotten to the point where it's definitely a Game of the Year contender - albeit a very low-key one.

Officially, what you're getting here is a "retro-fantasy action RPG with brutal combat and traversal-focused exploration", and Queen's Domain is being compared to loads of legendary franchises including King's Field, Zelda and Dark Souls.

Here's what just a few people are saying about it on Steam, for example:

cautious asparagus on Steam: "It's the kind of game that keeps surprising you with the sheer scope and creativity. You know the first time in Elden Ring where you find the elevator that brings you down to Siofra River, and you're just in awe of how much more there is to the game? There are multiple times in Queen's Domain where you feel that same way. This is the best RPG I have played this year, and it might even be my game of the year."

Huell Babineaux: "Everyone says this is one of the best kings field successors out there and it probably is, but ive never played those games, so to me this game feels more like a dark and gritty first person legend of zelda, and it pulls this off exceptionally well. Combat is brutal and unforgiving, but also learnable. Exploration can be daunting and overwhelming, but always rewarding.

Powersteve on Steam: My game of the year. Not just the best King's Field imitator but a genuine improvement on the formula. Better combat, better variety of combat options and a massive world with some of the best level and secret design I have ever seen. Also remains engaging and balanced for the whole duration and doesn't turn into Doom with lightning bolts half way through like Lunacid. So good that I can't wait to get all the endings just so I can use those secrets to do a fresh run with sequence breaks which is something that I almost never do.

So, why haven't we mentioned this before? Well, the Xbox version of Queen's Domain was actually getting a bit of flack at launch, as people were pointing out a stuttering issue that seemed to be plaguing the Series X and S versions.

Looking at the reviews on the Xbox Store now though, the issue seems to have been addressed in a recent patch, and Queen's Domain is currently rocking a 4.7/5 rating on the US version of the Xbox Store as things stand.

In other words, this might well be worth picking up for your Xbox console! It's £16.74 / $19.99 if you fancy taking a punt in the near future, and we'll leave you with more details and screenshots for it down below.

Queen’s Domain is a retro-fantasy action RPG. Washed up on the shores of the Isle of Neasied, you set out to find your father and uncover the dark heart of this mysterious isle. Wield the Legendary Holy Sword Endu to take flight from platform to platform, and discover an interconnected, labyrinthine world where secrets and dangers lurk around every corner.

Fight action-oriented battles with a classic stamina meter, powerful charge attacks, weapon specific special attacks, and secondary throwing weapons. Level up, accessorize, and choose from a huge catalogue of melee weapons on your quest to fight your way through the hordes of monsters and powerful bosses awaiting you in the darkest depths of the isle.

#4198. Ocarina Of Time Remake Is “Terrific”, Says GTA 6 Boss

I don't think gaming will ever recapture the pandemic high of Doom Crossing and all the fan-art that came with it, but Ocarina of Time is the only game that's dared to launch against GTA 6—ignoring the Aspyr special Shrek remaster—so it's hard not to lump the two together.

They have entirely different audiences and occupy entirely different platforms, and yet fans are leaning into the faux rivalry; there was even an SNL sketch about it. But what does Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick think about the game?

"It's terrific," he told GamesBeat. "They should be very proud of the title. In the entertainment business, you compete against everything and nothing. Everything because there's so many ways consumers can spend their time, and nothing because if there's nothing good out there, people don't need to consume any of it."

Zelnick says that games, like all entertainment, are not necessities like food. They're luxuries. It's up to companies like Take-Two to make the best games they possibly can to get people through the door.

"It's like food; food could be bad, but you still are going to be hungry," he explained. "But in the case of entertainment, it's not a must-have; it's a want to have. So, it's our job to make the best entertainment on Earth. When we do that, people will show up for it."

We’ve not even got GTA 6 yet, but Rockstar is already sharing its thoughts on what could come next.

GTA 6 is the most pre-ordered game of all-time, and has made nearly $1 billion in presales alone. Ocarina of Time, on the other hand, sold over 5.2 million copies in its first four days. Most publishers scrambled out of the way of GTA 6 this month, except for the awful Shrek remaster and, bizarrely, Barbie Rewind, but Ocarina of Time hasn't been hurt by the looming shadow of what is shaping up to be the biggest launch in gaming history—big enough to already be causing internet outages.

Like I said, they both have entirely different audiences, and Ocarina of Time is a Switch 2 exclusive—a platform you can't play GTA 6 on. They were never direct competitors, but the idea of a Grand Theft Ocarina mash-up rivalry is too fun to pass up.

#4197. Marathon may actually have a shot as Server Slam hits it big on Steam

Marathon's latest public open weekend has kicked off, and it looks like enough people have showed up to play it.

Things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next big game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

The Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

Immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game quickly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

These figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

Like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

Assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a big launch.

Marathon arrives March 5 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

#4196. The Switch 2 Pro Controller Can Make Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Even Better

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time hit Switch 2 today, and, as Kyle Hilliard pointed out in our review, it is pretty excellent. Along with its remarkable visual upgrade, the new Switch 2 remake of Ocarina of Time adds quality-of-life improvements and modernizes the control scheme. As part of that, Nintendo has added the ability to jump and sprint. While that works well to make the game feel new, I quickly realized it sometimes clashes with another new improvement: a free camera controlled by the right stick. Holding down the sprint button to get through areas as fast as possible can make it tricky to keep the camera where you want it, but thankfully, if you have the Switch 2 Pro Controller, there's an easy fix.

After hours of running around, I was awestruck by the level of detail and updates, but I found myself constantly fighting with the camera, or at the very least, needing to take a strange claw-style grip to be able to direct the camera with the right stick, while holding down the A button to sprint. If you're a casual Switch 2 player, you might not have even noticed the back buttons on the Pro Controller, or you just have no idea what they do. Those buttons can be remapped on a per-game basis and it's a simple process. Everyone has their own preferences, but, for example, for high-mobility shooters, I like remapping one of those to reload and one to jump. I've never felt the need to remap in a Zelda game, but after feeling the need to do so with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2, I might do so going forward.

If you, like me, struggle to comfortably steer the new free camera while running through hallways, towns, dungeons, and, yes, Hyrule Field, you might want to consider remapping your controller. As you can see in the above image, the placement of Jump and Dash on the face buttons can make it difficult to simultaneously control the camera and sprint. This isn't typically a problem in most modern games, as clicking the right stick is often a toggle to sprint, but in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2, you need to hold the button.

If you have the Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller, copying one button's functionality to the buttons on the back of the controller is simple. All you need to do is hold the Home button on the Switch 2 Pro Controller for a moment until the Switch 2 system menu appears on the right side. Along with Power Options and any Bluetooth audio devices you have available, there is also the option to map GL and GR, the controller's back buttons on the left and right, respectively.

Navigate down the menu to the GL and GR, then select which one you'd like to map. It will ask you which button you want to assign to the one you selected. Everyone can choose whatever makes sense in their own head, but mapping A (Roll and Dash) to GL and X (Jump) to GR made the most sense to me. Now, while I'm using the Switch 2 Pro Controller, I can use my middle finger to hold the GL button to Dash around without removing my thumb from the camera-controlling right stick.

And the best part is that, since you're not removing the functionality of the A or X buttons, you can still use them when it makes sense. For example, A also controls actions like opening up a treasure chest or door, and in my head, that feels like a face-button action, whereas rolling and dashing feel right mapped to the back buttons. The only downside is that, since this functionality is new for Switch 2 Pro Controllers, it isn't available if you're using the Joy-Cons or a Switch 1 Pro Controller. Also, it can make switching over to handheld mode challenging, as you don't have access to the back buttons in that play style.

Even if you don't have the ability to take advantage of this tip, either because you don't own a Switch 2 Pro Controller or because you prefer playing in handheld mode, you should still absolutely play the Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. To learn more about the experience and why it's a must-play, head to our review.

Original Story: Remember Mouse Work? It was announced by developer Nitrome for the Switch 2 just a few months before the system's launch and requires you to use mouse controls to complete all sorts of fun and challenging jobs.

We've not got an update about this title since last year, but it looks like it's finally on the way. According to a listing that has recently appeared on the Japanese Nintendo Store and eShop, it will be arriving this holiday season on 7th December 2026 for 2,200 yen.

#4194. Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet Is A Combination Of Jak, Uncharted, And TLOU

In a new interview, Naughty Dog co-president Neil Druckmann has revealed that Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet is in the “final stages” of development and will be shown off next year.

When The Last of Us Part 2 released in 2020 and quickly became the best game that Naughty Dog has ever made (sorry, Uncharted 4), the studio’s next steps were more mysterious and exciting than ever. It was pretty clear that the team would leave The Last of Us behind for a bit and work on something new, which was heavily rumoured to be a fantasy adventure.

That turned out to be completely wrong, as it was revealed at the end of 2024 that Naughty Dog’s next game is Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, a sci-fi adventure that, even nearly two years after the reveal, we know almost nothing about. PlayStation fans have wondered for a while now just how long we’d be waiting, and it sounds like there’s not much more left to wait.

As pointed out by Twitter user Okami13_, Neil Druckmann recently appeared on the Comic Creators Block Party 2026 and took the chance to share some rare details about Intergalactic. During that talk, Druckmann confirmed that the game is in the “final stages” of development, and that gameplay and details will be shared next year.

Of course, considering how long we’ve waited for Intergalactic, it’s not that surprising to know we’ll actually see more of it in 2027, but it is noteworthy that it’s approaching the end of production. We already know that motion capture wrapped earlier in the year, so it sounds like a late 2027 release could actually be on the cards.

It would also make sense, since we really only know about Until Dawn 2 and Laufey for PlayStation’s big 2027 releases so far. Intergalactic as a bookmark for what could be the last year of this console generation seems fitting.

That wasn’t the only thing that Druckmann said, though, as he noted that Intergalactic is basically a “combination” of Jak and Daxter, Uncharted, and The Last of Us, since it takes elements of sci-fi adventure, action-adventure, and "serious drama". Sure, The Last of Us and Uncharted are baked into Naughty Dog’s DNA at this point, but hearing the name Jak in the big 2026 is a very nice surprise.

Two hours with Xenoverse 3’s Parallel Quests made me sure that the full game is absolutely going to ruin my life.

#4193. The Sims 4 is getting paid mods, and a new in-game currency to pay for them

The Sims 4 is about to launch a couple of major initiatives that may not exactly be what players have been looking for.

The Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis announced The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two new destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

The two new features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

Created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature launches, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

Alongside this, the game is also introducing a new virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

It is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

In order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

In the blog post announcing the new features, Maxis said that creators will have control over the price of their content, and how it's packaged. These are referred to as Maker Packs, which can include Create-a-Sim or Build/Buy items.

You can apply to become a Maker from March 5. Once accepted, you’ll also get access to the Maker Suite, which is what you’re going to use to test your work to ensure it runs smoothly on the different platforms, and eventually publish it.

#4192. 'The Biggest Launch In WoW History' - Xbox's Latest First-Party Game Is Already Smashing Records

Bodes well for that eventual console release, eh?

We've talked quite a bit recently about the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever on PC and how it may end up being the biggest success of the year from an Xbox first-party perspective, and it seems that could actually be the case.

Its PC launch happened back on November 4th, and according to the folks at The Game Business, it's already broken multiple records for the series, including the biggest launch in WoW history based on peak concurrent players.

Here's a look at those records that have been broken:

Many people might overlook the success of WoW: Forever for Team Xbox simply because it's not shipping on consoles (at least not yet), but we reckon Xbox CEO Asha Sharma will extremely pleased by the game's success thus far!

It does seem to bode well for an Xbox Series X|S and/or Xbox Project Helix version in the future too - there's seemingly little point leaving money on the table when the new game is already optimised for controllers as it is.

Obviously it's still early days for WoW: Forever and the initial success will inevitibly drop off, but if they can retain enough interest in the months and years to come, Xbox will have an excellent new money spinner on their hands.

A documentary is on the way, titled Massive Effect: The BioWare Story, will track the studio from its creation to its last two years. According to IGN, the documentary is produced by Shane Fennessey and Adam Scorgie and is being made for Canada‘s Super Channel and will release some time next year. BioWare was based in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada.

Geoff Keighley shared a few additional details about the upcoming documentary and confirmed his involvement as an interviewee.

Next year, the story of BioWare will be told in MASSIVE EFFECT: THE BIOWARE STORY, a new documentary that chronicles the history of the company and its sad closure by Electronic Arts. I was honored to be interviewed for it earlier this year. https://t.co/928LPZWK7H

— Geoff Keighley (@geoffkeighley) November 5, 2026

Late last month, news broke that EA was shuttering BioWare, the studio behind Mass Effect, Dragon Age, and more. Following the news, a work-in-progress teaser trailer leaked sharing what the team had been working on. Ea reportedly closed BioWare in favor of pursuing more Star Wars projects, which you can read about more here.

#4190. PSA: Nintendo Ending Google And Apple Sign-Ins On Nintendo Accounts In 2027

You'll need a Nintendo Account from here on out

If you currently use a Google or Apple account to sign in to your Nintendo Account, Nintendo has got some news. In an official notice, it's announced the discontinuation of Google and Apple account sign-ins on Nintendo Accounts.

This will take place on 26th January 2027, so we're just a few months out. "As of" this date, it will no longer be possible to link a Google or Apple account. Nintendo notes this exact end time "may be delayed depending on the progress of the system change work".

Nintendo: "We apologise for any inconvenience to those who used a Google or Apple account to sign in to their Nintendo Account."

Here's what this means when it does come into effect:

And "if you are already logged into your Nintendo Account on a device, you may not have to sign in again". If the sign-in page does appear, you'll need to sign in using the email address or sign-in ID and your password for your Nintendo Account, or a Passkey.

If we hear any updates about this, we'll let you know. What are your thoughts about this announcement? Let us know in the comments.

#4189. GTA 6 South Korean Age Rating Confirms Previous Leaks Were A Dev Build

South Korea almost refused to give Grand Theft Auto 6 an age rating due to the overwhelming amount of nudity “without context” that looked even worse thanks to Cyberleek.

I can’t believe we’re finally here, but we’re now officially one week away from the release of GTA 6. It’s been a long, long road, but things have finally started to feel real over the past few months as the game’s final trailers, marketing, collaborations, screenshot batches, and more have emerged to show just how far Rockstar’s marketing can go.

On the more official end, age-rating boards have started to share their ratings for GTA 6, unsurprisingly confirming that it’s getting the highest possible classifications across the board. That just about includes South Korea, which apparently almost outright refused to give the game a rating due in part to its “background genital exposure”.

As pointed out by ResetEra user TheAbsolution, Inven Global has shared a report on just how close GTA 6 got to being refused classification in South Korea. You might think that it’s because of the game’s more realistic violence or drug use, but that’s not the case, as the board deemed that it wasn’t too much more advanced than GTA 5.

Exactly how realistic is Rockstar's long-awaited Grand Theft Auto 6 going to be?

The problem lies with the game’s more frequent nudity, specifically without any “sexual context”, essentially referring to background characters who are naked in-game. One member of the board pointed out that the nudity was an issue because it “has never appeared this frequently without context” or with “narrative justification”.

The report also shows that there was some pressure to figure it out so that South Korea wasn’t the only country to refuse to give GTA 6 a rating.

South Korea’s rating board’s first meeting ended with a tie and resulted in a copy being given for review to evaluate “sensuality”. The board found that the “genital exposure scenes” appeared as one-offs in the background that didn’t lead to any interactions. The board even had to request a map from Take-Two multiple times to find the nudist gathering that was previously leaked.

Eventually, the decision was made to give GTA 6 an Adults Only rating, which was in part due to the infamous leaked nudity scenes from Cyberleek not being found in-game, confirming once and for all that it was a dev build hack and not meant to be seen. It’s not clear if any modifications ended up being made by Rockstar or Take-Two, but at least a classification has been issued.

We finally got a chance to play The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake and it's still one of the best games ever made.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#4188. Our first look at Diablo 4's Warlock and the game's next season arrive in today's livestream - watch it here

Diablo 4's latest Developer Update is nearly upon us, and it's one plenty of the game's fans and players have been looking forward to.

Diablo 4’s next, long-awaited Developer Update finally airs today. This meaty livestream was first announced nearly a month ago, when Blizzard initially revealed that the game’s next class is the Warlock.

The Warlock’s initial unveiling, however, was incredibly brief, showing no gameplay. It also didn't explain how the class is going to fit within the existing roster. This all changes today.

Blizzard is bringing back its Developer Update livestream programme, which is the more structured, information-dense series of developer showcases. The focus of this one, of course, is going to mainly be on the Warlock class.

The Warlock is one of two classes coming to Diablo 4 with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion. The first, the Paladin, is already available in the game for anyone who pre-orders the expansion. The Warlock will instead arrive alongside the expansion on April 28.

The Developer Update will also include a first look at the game’s next season (Season 12), currently set for March 10. This mini season will only last until the expansion’s release, so it’s going to be interesting to see what it brings to the game.

You’ll be able to watch the showcase live at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT on Diablo 4’s official YouTube, Twitch, and Twitter channels. We’ve embedded the YouTube and Twitch players below for your convenience.

Among the topics the Developer Update will cover are the Killstreaks system, as well as Bloodstained items. As always, you can also expect a Q&A segment at the end of the show, and I imagine there’s going to be a few about the Warlock.

#4187. Award-Winning Composer And Musician Jon Batiste Talks Ocarina Of Time's Music And Why 'Guile's Theme' Goes With Everything

Jon Batiste has collaborated with the likes of Alicia Keys, Lenny Kravitz, Prince, Stevie Wonder, Willie Nelson, and many more. He performed the national anthem at Super Bowl LIX. He's headed up the musical efforts of The Late Show with Stephen Colbert. He's taken home more awards than we can realistically list in this article (including eight Grammys, as well as an Academy Award, a BAFTA Award, and a Golden Globe). But as I sit down with Batiste for a brief conversation about video game music, his energy transcends the Zoom call.

Before I can even ask a question, Batiste begins singing to greet me, then nerds out about my NBA Jam and Street Fighter II cabinets. He begins humming the menu music from NBA Jam and reminiscing about all the quarters he pumped into his local Street Fighter cabinet. The Louisiana native and Juilliard School alum has been an ardent gaming enthusiast for nearly three decades, with compositions from games like Sonic the Hedgehog and Final Fantasy VII inspiring his earliest musical endeavors. Spend enough time watching video game music performances on social media, and you'll likely soon find videos of Batiste sitting with famed Final Fantasy composer Nobuo Uematsu, or of Batiste performing gaming music.

With The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time delivering some of the most iconic music of all time (and Batiste famously loving the music), it makes sense that Nintendo would bring him out to New York to serve as a special guest at the launch event for the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on Switch 2. I sat down with Batiste for a few minutes to chat about his love of video game music, his history with Nintendo, and why "Guile's Theme" from Street Fighter II just goes so well with everything.

Ocarina of Time is easily one of the most important video games ever made, and one of the things that makes it so special is the music. What about Ocarina of Time sticks out to you sonically?First off, if you want to get super inside baseball, technical music nerdery, which I love to do, in the compositions, there's a way that major chords and minor chords in... no sevenths, just root, third, fifth. They alternate, and it creates this magic that is, like, it's wistful, and it's simple. It feels ancient, and it feels like it's the music that is going on in your mind as you're generating thoughts and your imagination is churning. And the major chords are happening just after the minors in this contrary motion that's happening, so it feels like the music is going like this: It's going up – major, minor – like [sings the main Legend of Zelda theme song].

So, it's expanding and contracting, which is a musical allegory for the expansion and the openness of the world that Link is in. It's like [Koji Kondo] figured out how to capture the essence of the gameplay, but also the essence of magic and simplicity, which I think is really what makes... that's the music's power! So, you could listen to the music in the game, and you could also listen to it apart from the game and experience that magic.

Are there any tracks in Ocarina of Time that stand out to you as the most musically sophisticated or compositionally impressive?Oh man. Well, I think of it as a suite, so that's what makes it actually... there's nothing that's more or less complex, but the thought to figure out how to make all of the themes be interrelated yet singular. "Song of Storms" is, like, for me, that's a personal favorite. That's why I like to play it. I like to play a lot of the themes. That's how I grew up! I would play the game, and then, I would go to an instrument. Once we played for hours on Nintendo, we'd go and play Nintendo on piano! It was like a trade-off there, you know? I've been doing this since I was about 11 years old.

Taking it back to that 11-year-old Jon, talk to me a little bit about your history in general.Okay, so my history with Nintendo goes back to the NES. Christmas morning. Duck Hunt. You remember that? Maybe the first game I ever played. No, the first game I ever played was Donkey Kong, and then Duck Hunt, and then Super Mario Bros. Staples! We're talking about the early '90s. We had a room where I would go – it was my domain – and we had this blue shag carpet, and I would sit back there, and I would basically disappear into the carpet playing Nintendo for hours and hours.

And my mind is kind of... my mind can become a spiral; it can become a tornado. And I realized even then that going into this world of the game, even if I didn't win – it's not about winning or losing – it helps to organize the spiral of my mind and give me ideas and inspiration. So then, I started to get into Street Fighter II when I started to play more communally with my sister and my cousins. Yoko Shimomura, who I also had the pleasure of meeting and collaborating with, she composed incredible themes for each character, and that's when I really started to get a true love for fighting games.

And then, we would play so many of the Street Fighter franchise. We would play a lot of Final Fight. There were so many things... there was Double Dragon, then we got Mega Man... all these different series. Mega Man X is [an] all-time favorite. And then, here comes The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and that sort of expands the canon while also blending all of the elements: score, combat, the sort of linear quality of, like, a Donkey Kong or Super Mario World, and expanding the world in that way, expanding the canon in that way. Mind-blowing! So,  that sort of solidified my palate in terms of my favorite type of game.

You mentioned Street Fighter II. There's a meme about "Guile's Theme" and how it goes with everything. What about that composition makes it so it has the ability to enhance whatever video you pair it with?Wow! So, it has momentum in a way that is extremely [sings the melody of "Guile's Theme"] ... It draws you in, which is what you want [with] anything that you're starting when you're commencing a journey or watching something. You want it to draw you in, and that kind of pulls you in as that call and response. But it's an immediate announcement with the brass, and then the bass call and response. So, it's automatically giving you this feeling that something's happening, and I've got to pay attention to it! So that's the first step right there. And the tempo is really... it's a great tempo! It almost has the feeling of the great themes from, like, an '80s protagonist that's in a fighting movie. I think that was kind of the archetype. Yoko was probably drawing from that archetype, right? The action-hero archetype.

#4186. Poll: Xbox Turns 25 This Week, But Which Console Generation Had The Best Launch Titles?

This Sunday, Xbox will celebrate 25 years of great games and console experiences. Without giving away just how ancient we are, Fraser and I have been Xbox players since the beginning, enjoying each new generation of Xbox consoles and the games that launched alongside them.

With November 15th drawing closer, we thought we'd look back on each generation's launch lineup and ask for your verdict: which Xbox console had the best launch titles?

Was it the original Xbox, with Halo: Combat Evolved, Project Gotham Racing, and Fuzion Frenzy? How about the Xbox 360, with Condemned: Criminal Origins, Kameo: Elements of Power, and Call of Duty 2? Perhaps the Xbox One, with Ryse: Son of Rome, Dead Rising 3, and Forza Motorsport 5? Or is it the Xbox Series X|S, with Gears Tactics, Forza Horizon 4, and Sea Of Thieves?

We all have our favourite games from each console generation, but which one had the best launch lineup? That's for you to decide by voting in the poll below. Before you do, though, here's a closer look at each Xbox generation's launch titles:

On this page: Poll: Xbox Turns 25 This Week, But Which Console Generation Had The Best Launch Titles?

So, now you know which games launched with which Xbox consoles, and all that's left to do is vote! I reckon I can probably guess which console the PX community will favour, but who knows? Get voting!

#4185. Diablo 4's next season is short, but it lets you become The Butcher, and it has Doom: The Dark Ages skins you probably can't afford

Blizzard has unveiled the next Diablo 4 season, which kicks off next week to hold us over until the launch of the game's big expansion in April.

The big Diablo 4 Developer Update has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

Patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

When you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

Starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the new Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

If you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a new event that rewards you for killing enemies quickly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

Elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a new activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

The Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

Anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

There are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

The other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a new item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

Even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the new season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

The trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the new class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

Season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

The more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

#4184. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – November 6, 2026

This week and weekend is all about the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, one of the few games I feel deserves the title of masterpiece. And the remake is really well done! I got every heart piece, every Gold Skulltala, the Goron Sword, and the biggest pouch for every one of my items over the course of the review... but I am contemplating jumping right back in for another go.

We also revealed our next cover and in case you missed the announcement it is... pause for effect... Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis! It's an awesome cover that celebrates the history of Lara Croft, and along with a cover story on the game, we also have a big retrospective on the series. I highly recommend subscribing to get your issue if you haven't already.

But it wasn't all just Zelda and Tomb Raider this week. Below you will find a list of weekend play recommendations, but before that... some of our biggest stories of the week.

We have been writing a lot about The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time remake this week because it is one of 2026's most exciting games, and it's real good. The remake is not particularly surprising. It mostly sticks to the trajectory of the original game, but there is a reason it is considered one of the best games of all time. It also looks and plays amazing.

You can read the full review here (or watch the video above), but we also have a big interview with the game's producers (one of whom worked on the original Ocarina of Time, and one who directed Breath of the Wild among many other Zelda games), some details about the Easter Eggs that did and did not make it into the remake, and a very handy tip for the game if you happen to be playing with a Switch 2 Pro controller.

World of Warcraft: Forever is out now and it’s a great time to jump into the revamped and expanded version of a project that changed online games forever back in 2004. A thousand new quests, multiple new zones, countless revamps, and an impressively stunning visual overhaul make it the perfect time to jump in for anyone who’s ever been curious to explore Azeroth.

2022's Escape Academy was a sneaky little puzzle game that surprised me and its sequel released this week. Taking place in a school obsessed with puzzles, you play as a student who must make their way through a series of escape rooms. The puzzles are clever, and the setting is charming, but the secret weapon is the local, split-screen co-op. Solving puzzles together is fun especially when one player needs to look at one section of a room to help dictate a solution on the other side of the room. My wife and I both love video games, but rarely play co-op games together just because of our disparate, individual tastes. But Escape Room is one we enjoyed together and we're so far enjoying the sequel. My only complaint so far is... I wish it ran a little better.

While we collectively use the term here for the sake of familiarity, I’m always a bit hesitant in my own mind to label a game under the wide banner of “Metroidvania.” In part, that’s because I think the two referenced games (Metroid and Castlevania: Symphony of the Night) are actually more different than they might appear at first glance. Gloomsoft’s recent release, Moadra, recognizes that distinction, crafting a game that draws heavy inspiration from the specific tradition of Super Metroid, even while presenting an intriguing and atmospheric fiction that is great fun to discover. In movement, actions, and exploration, Moadra feels remarkably similar to  the best of the 2D Metroid games. A scanning tool also leans into the Metroid inspirations, revealing details about the weird alien world you’re navigating. If you’ve been hungry for a game that scratches that particular itch of sci-fi gear/ability-gated exploration, I think you’ll find a lot to love in this game.

I get the Marvel fatigue we've all been experiencing. There are a lot of games and a lot of movies and a lot of TV shows and many are good, but lately most feel like homework. For those reasons, you'd be forgiven for dismissing the 2021 Guardians of the Galaxy game, but I promise you it is good. For one, it is standalone. It does not directly tie to any specific Marvel media. No homework necessary. And for two, it's just a really good game with an affecting story and a unique take on the characters that most of us met for the first time in the movies. And, for the BioWare fans out there mourning the loss of Mass Effect, this game has some Mass Effect energy. It's available on Switch 2 this week and I happily recommend it, especially if you missed it five years ago.

This exclusively two-player board game features a fun mix of activities. You act as both a dungeon architect, and an adventurer delving into said dungeons. Each player creates their own version of a challenging dungeon filled with traps, monsters, and treasures.

But you’re also forced to take on the dangers of your opponent’s crafted dungeon, to see who manages to come out on top. If you have fond memories of the hidden-info nature of old games like Battleship, but you want some greater strategic depth and fantasy flavor thrown in, this one is a great pick.

#4183. Unknown 'Mega Man Legends' Project Surfaces Online

Update [Thu 12th Nov 2026, 2:30am]: In an update, the 'Mega Man Legends' listing on ACTRA Toronto's "What's Shooting" database has now been removed (via Rockman Corner).

Original Story: As Capcom gears up for Mega Man's 40th anniversary next year, more findings related to the long-running IP are surfacing online.

As reported by Mega Man fan site Rockman Corner, a production titled 'Mega Man Legends' has appeared on ACTRA Toronto's "What's Shooting" database (a public listing of production registered with the Canadian performers' union) this week.

It's filed under "new media" and the production start date was in September, with it scheduled to wrap up by December. Casting is apparently in house, but that's all that's known about the mysterious project.

As the source notes, "new media" could be everything from "video games to television and film". It's also mentions how Capcom "could be looking to Canadian voice talent as an alternative to SAG-AFRA Actors" after "Mega Man: Dual Override became the subject of a SAG-AFTRA 'Do Not Work' order" earlier this year.

Mega Man Legends was originally released as a 3D video game in 1997 and was followed by a second game in 2000. There was also a prequel spin-off in 1999, and a cancelled third entry for the 3DS.

This latest finding also follows a rating board classification in Korea at the end of last month. It featured various classic Capcom console titles, including multiple Mega Man games.

#4182. How To Get In The Same Phase In World Of Warcraft: Forever

Stop losing friends to phasing in World of Warcraft: Forever — quick world refresh tips to get your party back in Azeroth.

Playing World of Warcraft: Forever with friends is a great way to tackle difficult quests and explore Azeroth. However, joining the same party doesn't always mean you can see each other.

The game uses multiple copies of outdoor zones, commonly called phases or layers, to manage its player population. Because of this, you might find yourself standing in the same location as a party member without being able to see or interact with them. Fortunately, you can move into the same phase without leaving your party.

When you join a party, look near your chat window for a blue notification stating that the world around you will refresh. This message may include a countdown, but you don't have to wait for the timer to expire.

If you previously dismissed the notification, look for a small arrow near your chat window to reopen it.

Unlike some earlier versions of World of Warcraft, joining a party doesn't automatically move you into the same phase as the rest of your party. The refresh system lets you choose when to make that transition.

It's best to refresh somewhere safe because enemies may appear in different locations after changing phases.

Hide your secondary name in World of Warcraft: Forever — quick nameplate steps to keep only your main name visible.

If you're still having trouble joining your friends, here are a few things that have helped me while playing with friends.

First, crossing a zone boundary can trigger a phase change and put your party members into the same version of the world.

When that doesn't work, log out and back in while remaining in the party. This also helped my party members appear on the same phase as everyone else.

Once everyone is visible, you can finally get back to questing together instead of wondering why your friends have vanished into another dimension. If you run into the same problem later, check for the World Refresh notification before leaving your party. There’s usually no reason to disband your group just to get everyone together.

#4180. Diablo 4’s Warlock looks like an unhinged Necromancer with Sorcerer energy in first look at gameplay

Diablo 4's practitioner of forbidden arts, The Warlock, has been officially unveiled as the second class coming with Lord of Hatred.

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Update, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

Since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Update to actually see it in action.

The Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

The Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

The Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

The Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside new Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

Lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the big day.

#4179. New Details Revealed About The Physical Edition Of GTA 6 For Xbox Series X|S

Double-sided poster, shipping dates & more

Everyone already knows about the code-in-a-box situation for GTA 6's physical edition on Xbox Series X|S and PS5, but we've also come to learn a few extra details in recent days about what to expect from the boxed copy of the game.

So, when you open up GTA 6 for Xbox Series X|S in physical form, you'll be presented with a code that will allow you to redeem the game on the Microsoft Store - essentially converting your physical purchase into a digital one.

Rockstar Games mentioned a shipping date of November 12th for the physical version a few days ago, but we've spotted some retailers saying they'll start shipping on the 11th instead, while a very small number of people even seem to have their copy already.

Once you've got the physical version in your hands, you'll be able to preload GTA 6 in full, although you can technically also do that from tonight by installing the game via the Xbox mobile app.

As you can also see from the tweet above, the physical edition is now confirmed to come with a double-sided A3 poster (at least if you buy from certain retailers). This poster appears to include the game's main artwork along with some character art on the back, so that's at least a nice little bonus to ease the pain of a disc-less release.

But what about a map? Well, Rockstar Games is handling the map a bit differently this time around, making a digital version available to download for free at launch. Alternatively, physical maps will be available to buy from the Rockstar Store "shortly after launch" for $0.99, but we reckon those will be in extreme demand and quickly sell out.

Of course, none of this really changes the fact that the physical edition of GTA 6 is kinda pointless for any platform as things stand, but it does at least make for a good display piece, and it'll be popular for gifting purposes this Christmas.

What's even weirder about this is that Rockstar is supporting GTA 6's launch with various other physical releases, such as an official soundtrack album and all kinds of merch, but it seems there's little hope for a disc version right now.

#4178. Round Up: The Reviews Are In For Pikmin 4 - Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy

Following the anticipated return of Zelda: Ocarina of Time last week, Nintendo has now released Pikmin 4 - Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy. The critic reviews have now gone live. If you haven't already seen ours, we gave it seven stars, calling it a pleasant but perplexing piecemeal.

"Overall, £8/$10 is a small price to pay for some minor new features and a fun little mode that'll keep me entertained over the coming year, but it's more of a budding shoot right now than the full-bloom upgrade."

Mini Review Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy (Switch 2) - Pleasant But Perplexingly Piecemeal

And here's what other critics had to say:

"For late-bloomers who have yet to experience the magic that is Pikmin 4, the Nintendo Switch 2 Edition is the best place to start. Not only is native 4K resolution a significant improvement that allows the colourful world of Pikmin to shine brighter than ever before, Dandori Academy brings some worthwhile new content, held back only by Nintendo’s puzzling monthly stage distribution method. While not quite as extravagant as some of the other Nintendo Switch 2 Editions we’ve seen in recent memory, the lower-end $10 for the Upgrade Pack is an appropriate price point for what Pikmin 4 has to offer on Nintendo Switch 2; with the base game being in a class of its own."

"The main takeaway is that Pikmin 4 is still excellent, and I was grateful to transfer my save file from the Switch version (and I was tempted to start a new game + save), but Dandori Academy is not a strong incentive to return if you already played the game. It is a nice bonus and an interesting concept that reimagines the familiar time trial mode featured in plenty of video games, but the original campaign is still the main attraction."

"Pikmin 4 still remains one of my favourite titles released on the original Nintendo Switch, but unfortunately this update has left me feeling more than a little underwhelmed. While the game has seen a visual upgrade and the Oatchi commands are certainly a novel addition, the drip-feeding of its major new Dandori Academy content proves more frustrating than anything. More Pikmin is never a bad thing, but having to wait months to see it all, well… that’s a drag."

"Pikmin 4 is already a great time; Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy is just the 4K cherry on top. If you don’t own the original Switch version, then this is an easy recommendation; if you’re here for the upgrade/additions, then the visual upgrade will help. Dandori Academy won’t be for everyone, but over the next year it will continue to add extra challenges. The cheaper upgrade price point helps make it an easier recommendation."

PSA 'Pikmin 4 + Dandori Academy' Demo Blooms On Switch 2 Today

I think this is just part of a wider discussion about how games are reviewed in 2026 when more and more games launch in an unfinished state, or with a promise of a long content roadmap. Admittedly this is more of a rarity with Nintendo games specifically as they tend to be a lot more traditional in how games are packaged and released as complete items.

I suppose what I’m interested in is whether the lovely folks at Nintendo life plan on revisiting this when all the content has been released and they can assess the full package. Or will interest have waned entirely be that point? Be interesting to see.

Pikmin is the best and I can't wait to let go of remakes and get to P5! Yeah!!

Unless they update the game to run at 60FPS, I wont be touching the update.

#4177. Best Classes To Play Solo In World Of Warcraft: Forever

Discover the best classes for solo play in World of Warcraft: Forever—why Hunters and Warlocks shine.

You won't always have someone available to quest with in World of Warcraft: Forever, so it's worth picking a class that can hold its own. While every class can reach level 60 solo, some make the journey a lot easier than others.

Hunters can send their pets into battle to tank for them, while Paladins have healing spells to get themselves out of trouble. Other classes, like Rogues, can sneak past enemies and avoid unnecessary fights. It’s also worth considering when each class unlocks its more useful abilities, as some take longer than others to reach their full potential.

Here are my five recommended classes for solo players in World of Warcraft: Forever, including the best leveling specializations and key Forever-specific changes.

One of the biggest advantages of playing a Rogue is that you don't have to fight everything in your path. With Stealth, you can sneak past enemies to reach quest objectives, saving yourself time and potentially a few frustrating deaths.

Taking down a single enemy is rarely the problem for a Rogue. However, you’ll be in trouble when another enemy wanders into the fight, especially if you’ve already used your defensive abilities. I recommend picking off enemies individually and using Stealth to avoid crowded areas whenever possible. There’s no reason to fight half the zone just to collect a quest item.

Combat is recommended for solo leveling, as it provides consistent single-target damage and talents that improve your weapon attacks and survivability.

Your general strategy is to open fights from Stealth, generate Combo Points with abilities like Sinister Strike, and spend them on finishers such as Eviscerate. You can also use Gouge to control an enemy when you need breathing room.

Rogues also received some welcome changes in World of Warcraft: Forever. For starters, Sap no longer breaks Stealth, so you can temporarily disable an enemy without revealing yourself. Poisons have more charges, too, and you can use them alongside temporary weapon enhancements.

You'll also pick up a couple of useful abilities as you level. At level 18, Posed reduces the Energy cost of your next ability when you reach full Energy outside combat. At level 24, Shank gives you another attack that generates Energy, helping you keep attacking instead of waiting for your Energy to recover.

However, Rogues struggle when fighting multiple enemies at once. They lack reliable self-healing and depend on defensive cooldowns, crowd control, and careful positioning to survive.

Combat is a great option if you enjoy picking your battles, but it takes more patience than classes that can comfortably fight multiple enemies at once.

World of Warcraft: Forever is finally live, and while it can be a bit intimidating to start, we've got a few tips to help you out!

One of the best reasons to play a Druid is that you can change how you fight without switching classes. If you’re facing a tough enemy, Bear Form gives you extra protection. Need to get somewhere without fighting everything along the way? Cat Form lets you sneak past enemies instead.

Feral Combat is the recommended solo spec, which focuses on melee damage, mobility, and survivability through Cat Form and Bear Form.

However, Druids can feel relatively slow during the early levels. Bear Form becomes available at level 10, but Cat Form doesn't unlock until level 20. This is where leveling with Feral becomes considerably more enjoyable.

At level 20, you’ll use Energy to attack instead of mana when you unlock Cat Form. This leaves your mana available for healing between fights. As you gain more abilities, you can apply a bleed effect with Rake, use Claw to generate Combo Points, and finish enemies off with your stronger attacks.

Feral Swiftness improves your movement in Cat Form. You can also use Prowl to sneak past unnecessary enemies, similar to a Rogue.

World of Warcraft: Forever also introduces several shapeshifting improvements. Your weapon's damage now contributes directly to your attacks in animal forms, while weapon enhancements and many consumables work without requiring you to transform back.

Additionally, the new Shifting Power talent lets you convert mana into Energy, helping you maintain offensive momentum later in the leveling process.

If an encounter becomes overwhelming, you can switch to Bear Form for additional durability or leave your animal form to heal.

Feral Combat is recommended if you want a class that can handle a little bit of everything. You’ll have plenty of options for getting out of trouble, although learning when to switch forms takes some getting used to.

Unlearn professions in WoW: Forever safely—what resets, how to relearn, plus a UI scale fix if the button's missing.

Paladins are the most forgiving classes for solo players because they combine heavy armor, healing spells, and powerful defensive abilities. You have several ways to recover without relying on another player should you find yourself in a bad situation.

Retribution is the recommended specialization for solo players. You'll focus on melee damage while maintaining the class's defensive strengths.

World of Warcraft: Forever introduces Holy Strike at level six, giving you an instant weapon attack that deals Holy damage. This helps improve early leveling, when Paladin combat can otherwise feel relatively slow.

The Seal and Judgement system has also received an important improvement in Forever. Judgement no longer consumes your active Seal, so you can maintain its effects without repeatedly spending mana to reactivate it.

Your general strategy is to maintain an offensive Seal, use Holy Strike and Judgment to damage enemies, and heal yourself when necessary.

Later in the Retribution talent tree, Twist of Light provides another offensive option. This talent lets your previous Seal temporarily carry over when you activate a different one so that you can benefit from two damage-dealing Seals on your next melee attack.

Protection is another option, particularly if you enjoy fighting multiple enemies. Consecration is now available to every Paladin at level 20, providing area damage that is especially effective against the first four targets.

Retribution is best for questing because most quests have you fighting enemies one at a time, so killing them faster is usually more efficient. You’ll still have access to healing spells and defensive abilities that can save you should you get into a sketchy situation.

Pirate Software’s OnlyFangs raid controversy just got put on blast in a new WoW: Forever trailer.

Warlocks are great for solo players because they can summon demons to fight alongside them while using powerful spells to defeat enemies from a distance.

Affliction is recommended because it is the most efficient leveling specialization, thanks to its combination of damage-over-time effects, self-healing, and resource management.

At level 10, Warlocks can obtain the Voidwalker, giving you a tank that draws enemy attention. This allows you to apply Corruption and Bane of Agony while your demon tanks incoming damage.

World of Warcraft: Forever introduces several improvements that make Affliction more effective. Damage-over-time effects can now crit, while talents like Malediction increase their damage.

The game also separates damaging Banes from utility Curses, allowing you to maintain a Bane of Agony alongside a Curse that weakens your enemies.

However, Affliction's biggest advantage for solo leveling is its ability to sustain itself through consecutive encounters. You can use Drain Life to restore your health, and Life Tap when you need an emergency mana refill.

Affliction also performs well against multiple enemies because you can spread damage-over-time effects across several targets while repositioning.

At level 40, Wrack provides another powerful offensive option. This new Affliction talent channels Shadow damage while making your active Corruption, Siphon Life, and Bane of Agony effects deal periodic damage 100 percent faster.

Affliction is the best choice for general questing because its damage-over-time spells and draining abilities allow you to move between enemies with minimal recovery time. It also lets you fight multiple enemies at once when needed.

Hide your secondary name in World of Warcraft: Forever — quick nameplate steps to keep only your main name visible.

Hunters are the top recommendation for solo players in World of Warcraft: Forever, thanks to their combination of ranged damage, mobility, and animal companions.

Beast Mastery is the recommended specialization. This spec allows you to focus on improving your pets' strength, durability, and damage.

The real fun starts at level 10, once you complete the pet-taming quest chain. Instead of fighting enemies at melee range, your pets will tank for you. You can now attack from a safe range.

Let your pet generate threat before you start shooting. Otherwise, you might find yourself dealing with an angry enemy running straight toward you. Serpent Sting works well against tougher enemies that will survive long enough to take damage over time, while Arcane Shot is useful when you need some immediate damage. If you’re fighting several enemies, make sure your pet isn’t taking more damage than it can handle.

Your pets now gain additional stats from your equipment, meaning your companion gets stronger as you upgrade your gear. This helps keep your pet useful throughout the leveling process.

Beast Mastery also receives new and redesigned talents. Focused Fire improves damage dealt by you and your pet, while Endurance Training increases your pet's durability.

A new ability, Summon Hawk, becomes available after you spend 16 talent points in Beast Mastery. This ability summons a hawk that temporarily attacks your target.

Hunters get improvements to their baseline abilities. Aimed Shot is now available to every Hunter at level 20, while traps can be placed during combat, giving you additional ways to control enemies.

Later, Bestial Wrath provides a powerful offensive cooldown that increases your pet's effectiveness against difficult opponents.

However, Hunters still need to keep their distance, as ranged attacks become unavailable when targets are too close. You must also manage your pet's health, positioning, and abilities.

The Beast Mastery spec offers one of the smoothest solo-leveling experiences available. Your pet can handle much of the danger while you deal consistent damage, making Hunter an excellent choice whether you're new to WoW or jumping from Retail to Forever.

Hunter or Warlock are the best choices if you’re planning to spend most of your time playing solo. Your pet will tank for you, which makes questing a lot less frustrating. Paladin is the best pick if you prefer melee classes instead. With heavy armor and healing spells, you can survive when you pull more enemies than you intended.

It’s also worth giving your chosen class some time before deciding whether to stick with it. Druids, for example, don’t unlock Cat Form until level 20, while Hunters have to reach level 10 before taming their first pet. A class that may feel slow at the beginning might become one of your favorites once you’ve unlocked more of its abilities.

#4176. Marathon launch player numbers are about half those of the Server Slam, at least on PC

Marathon hasn't quite been able to attract the same volume of players the recent Server Slam did.

After a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next big game has officially launched. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

The open test was largely well-received, and players actually showed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

In Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Marathon has now officially launched, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

Numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

Indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game currently sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.
